The evidence suggests that Spermine acts as a target for both [(Z)-(3-hydroxy-4-methoxyphenyl)methylideneamino]thiourea and spermidine, which in turn target ME-180. This indicates that Spermine may serve as a common precursor or modulator in the signaling pathways leading to ME-180 activation. The presence of two distinct compounds with overlapping targets further supports the idea that Spermine could influence ME-180 through a shared mechanism, possibly involving the sodium channel protein type 11 subunit alpha. The integration of these findings highlights the potential role of Spermine in modulating ME-180 activity, though the exact nature of this interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
